audit.summary: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated global step-size conditions: a finite two-state MDP with fixed stationary uniform behavior visits all four state-action pairs infinitely often but the learned greedy policy is suboptimal forever. Exact reachability iteration remains supportable. Local released PER weighting, numerical interpretation, Circle safety specification and README dispatch problems are Minor; historical empirical effects remain unresolved.

P1 — Global step-size assumptions do not imply sampled optimal convergence — Counterevidence: Behavior is fixed stationary and all pair frequencies positive, eliminating nonstationary/rare-visit objections. Step sequence is not nonincreasing, but monotonicity is not stated. Standard per-visit schedules would exclude the example. Exact reachability theorem and empirical curves are not refuted by it.

P2 — Classic-control importance weighting broadcasts over the batch — Counterevidence: Prioritized sampling remains. Highway branch explicitly squeezes residuals and is unaffected. No publication-time code binding or benchmark impact demonstrated. Actual tensor library diagnostic unavailable in checked runtimes.

P3 — Numerical summaries and blanket dominance contradict the tables — Counterevidence: Overall first/second SWU ordering survives. Table1 versusTable4 Roundabout differences are explained by comparison-set minimum target changing from.055 to.047; not an independent contradiction.

P4 — Circle unsafe-set inequality reverses the stated safety classification — Counterevidence: Released code agrees with inside-safe prose, so actual experimental inversion is not established. Crash reward differs between paper(-1) and current config(-10), with historical settings unknown.
P5 — README Circle command selects a reward-shaping baseline — Counterevidence: README Merge command explicitly selects sp_perdqn and is consistent. Historical publication commands remain unknown.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: Global step sum diverges, square sum=1/768+pi^2/6-1 is finite and beta tends to zero. Total step weight at x is only1/16. All safety values remain0; masks are full and kappa-gap condition is vacuous. Q in[0,2] invariant; Q(x,g)<=1/8 while Q(x,b)>=15/32 on every sample path. True Q values are4/3,1/3 at x and2/3 at y.

Recorded check: Broadcast multiplication yields(B,B), loss mean(e_i^2)*mean(w_j) rather than mean(w_i*e_i^2). For e=(1/4,3/4),w=(1,1/2), actual loss15/64 versus11/64; gradients(3/16,9/16) versus(1/4,3/8). Static shapes and primary PyTorch documentation checked; scalar arithmetic independently executed.

Recorded check: Table1 proposed row means .975,.738333 support .98,.74, not prose .90,.79. Table4 has .95,.73. TwoWay favors PER(.98>.88), Merge favors SPOM(.95>.94). TwoWay reward10.124/10.520 is below SafeQ10.636; SPOM Roundabout crash.167 exceeds SafeQ.090.

Recorded check: Printed S_u={abs(x)<=2.5} labels x0 unsafe and x3 safe; released cost/termination uses abs(x)>2.5.

Recorded check: Default algo is priorrewsdqn and the entrypoint dispatches to PriorRewsDQN. Its main block does not parse overrides. README claims the command is SPOM_PER.

assumptions: Finite states x,y with two actions g,b, deterministic alternation under both; gamma=1/2, rho concentrated at x; unsafe set empty (allowed). Reward r(x,g)=1, all others zero. Fixed stationary uniform independent behavior; all four pairs have limiting frequency 1/4 almost surely. psi0=0; Q0(x,b)=1/2 and others zero; no zero-Q initialization requirement. beta_2n=2^(-(n+5)), beta_(2n+1)=1/(n+2).

Safety residuals have shape(B,1); sampled weights have shape(B), with B>1 and nonconstant valid weights. Example current values(.30,.80), targets(.05,.05) yield residuals(.25,.75) in admissible bounds.
Compare printed conditions and means; no statistical-significance inference from small differences.
x_max=2.5; intended constraint is to remain inside the two walls.
Run the advertised bare entrypoint with preserved defaults, no unstated file changes.
